name: task-113-posting-prune-ab-intel-local
comment: Task 113 posting-scan bound-prune A/B. NON-STANDARD config (justified): the canonical lane sweep has no posting_bound_prune on/off A/B. One RaBitQ IVF index per scale; the A/B is driven by the per-step session_guc ec_ivf.posting_bound_prune = on|off, everything else held fixed so recall, ordering, and counters are directly comparable. EXPECTED RESULT: recall@10 and ordering byte-identical between arms (the Cauchy-Schwarz cutoff is a sound upper bound — pruning is a pure work reduction, proven recall-safe by test_ec_ivf_posting_bound_prune_equals_unpruned). The win is fewer postings scored / candidates retained and lower latency on high-recall (high-nprobe) cells; pruned-by-bound count rises with the arm on. recall/latency steps use the standard ec_ivf nprobe default_sweep [8,16,24,32,48,64] verbatim (profiles.rs). ENV-BLOCKED on this dev/review box (no staged corpora at data/staged-current/, no ecaz binary); run on the Intel bench desktop after staging ec_real_100k. Evidence Requirements to read off results.jsonl per cell: recall@10, NDCG@10, p50/p95/p99/mean, postings_visited, postings_scored, postings_pruned_by_bound, candidates_retained.

steps.name: precheck-host
args: SELECT now() AS captured_at, version() AS postgres_version, current_setting('shared_buffers') AS shared_buffers, current_setting('ec_ivf.posting_bound_prune') AS posting_bound_prune_default;
